name: Sprocket
text: Do it: Build a self-review loop where every prompt update triggers an automated review of the same task batch we used to tune it. This keeps the prompt sharp without manual checks. Trade-off: slower tuning cycles if the review runs long, but we cut human error and stale artifacts.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t just slower tuning cycles—it’s that a fresh batch of 500 tasks after the prompt update could fail silently because the review loop only checks the *same* batch it tuned from. A better alternative: run the review on a *random* 10% of the new batch before auto-applying, with a human sign-off if the error rate spikes. Settle it by testing both: compare failure rates between static and random sampling over two weeks.

name: Gauge
text: Gauge: The real risk isn’t just delayed deployment—it’s that testing 500 tasks *after* the prompt update could still miss drift because the new batch might share hidden biases with the old one. A better alternative: run the review on a *stratified* 10% sample that forces coverage of edge cases the old batch didn’t expose, with a human sign-off on the worst 5% of failures. Settle it by comparing failure rates on a held-out set of 1,000 tasks before and after the change.
